gap: eis-brasher-kingsbury-water-uptake-admissibility-v1 REFUTES H0 on all 6 physical screens: the USBR-21019 single-frequency 0.01 Hz EIS summary (|Z|, phase only) cannot support the Brasher-Kingsbury (1954) coating water-uptake law. Median dissipation factor 0.74 (only 14.3% of records capacitance-dominated, so no coating capacitance is readable at 0.01 Hz); log10 C_eff is Spearman -0.9921 with log10|Z| (rank-redundant, zero new information); 26.1% of derived uptakes are negative and 3.0% exceed the film volume; panel-to-panel reproducibility propagates to sigma(phi_v)=0.67 volume fraction, 2.2x the entire 0-30 vol% physical range. The module needs FREQUENCY-RESOLVED complex spectra Z'(f), Z''(f) with a high-frequency (>=1 kHz) coating-capacitance plateau, a pre-immersion dry C_0, plus specimen area and dry-film thickness, to unlock any water-uptake / equivalent-circuit / Kramers-Kronig capability. Note the Brasher-Kingsbury law is area- and thickness-free (capacitance RATIO only), so the missing USBR area does NOT explain the failure - the frequency resolution does.
